They call `stripped = line.strip()` and then check for block starts using `_DIRECTIVE_START_RE.match(stripped)` and `_starts_new_block(stripped)`. FOLLOW: In `_split_packet_directives`, shattered sub-items become independent blocks. `_prune_packet_directives` will prune them independently from the bottom up, leaving parent directives with missing sub-items. `resolve_layer_conflicts` will assign these sub-items their own priority and reorder them away from their parent directive. In `_apply_phenotype_transform`, shattered sub-items are treated as separate blocks and fail to collapse into a single line with their parent directive, violating the "concise" format style.
ANALYSE: HARD constraint (logic error). Premise: Indented list items belong to the parent directive block and are not top-level directives. Conclusion: Stripping leading whitespace before checking for a new block marker causes indented list items to be falsely identified as top-level blocks. CONFIRMED.
